title: Edge Metric Bridge: Admission and Shaping Policy for Inference KPIs
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Edge inference nodes currently emit a high-cardinality mix of Prometheus and OTLP metrics which floods the central ingestion pipeline and causes spikes in storage and query latency. There is no standard admission layer at the edge to enforce label hygiene, sample or compress metric envelopes, or attach trace hooks for request-level correlation. This leads to tenant billing unpredictability and noisy SLO breaches in latency dashboards.

Proposal: Implement an "Edge Metric Bridge" — a light-weight admission and shaping component that runs as a sidecar or small daemonset on inference nodes. Responsibilities: canonicalize labels (prefix rules, stable keys), drop or rewrite disallowed labels, collapse high-cardinality tag sets into canonical buckets, run tenant-aware sampling and dynamic cardinality throttling, attach span references (trace_id/span_id) to metric envelopes, and output both OTLP and Prometheus remote_write with a compact envelope format. The bridge should expose a small control plane endpoint for policy updates and local health/readiness.

Goals: Reduce central metric ingestion load by at least 60% for noisy tenants; preserve accuracy for SLO-critical KPIs (p95/p99 latency, error_rate, token_cost); enable per-request trace <-> metric linkage; provide rollout gating with feature flags and canary nodes.

Acceptance criteria: 1) Edge bridge successfully rewrites incoming metrics according to the canonicalization rules (test vectors provided) and emits expected reduced cardinality labels. 2) Integration test demonstrates 60% reduction in unique metric series across a synthetic noisy-workload. 3) OTLP envelopes include trace_id and span_id fields for at least 90% of request-correlated metrics in canary nodes. 4) No regression in p50 latency telemetry and <5% added CPU overhead on a standard inference node (8 vCPU) measured over a 1-hour load test. 5) Feature-flagged rollout mechanism and a rollback path documented in deployment runbook.

Implementation notes: - Language: Go (follow edge-sidecar conventions used by existing observability sidecars). - Hook into OTel SDK by registering a custom Metric Exporter that forwards to the admission pipeline. For Prometheus instrumented apps, provide a prometheus-proxy that accepts scraper pushes and translates to the same internal envelope. - Admission policy is rule-based JSON served from ConfigMap for K8s and a small file for on-prem. Rules include label_whitelist, label_rename_map, high_cardinality_patterns (regex), sample_rate_overrides_by_metric, tenant_capacity_fraction. - Compression: apply sketching for histograms and t-digest downsampling for percentile-oriented series, and use deterministic exemplar selection policy for traces. - Backpressure handling: when the bridge detects downstream saturation it will enter a graceful degrade mode that increases sampling and collapses labels to tenant-level. - Observability: the bridge emits its own health metrics (admitted_series_count, dropped_series_count, compression_ratio, avg_processing_ms) and debug logs at trace level.

Data contract: The bridge translates both OTLP metric point and Prometheus time-series into a canonical envelope: tenant_id, metric_name, canonical_labels (k=v pairs stringified), value, timestamp, trace_ref (trace_id/span_id optional), schema_version. The schema will be in Confluence link in attachments.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy bridge in canary on 5% of inference nodes (internal customers only) with full logging. 2) Run parallel-export to central pipeline + local-internal aggregator for 72 hours to compare cardinality and accuracy. 3) Iterate policies for noisy tenants. 4) Progressive ramp to 100% with per-tenant opt-outs.

Runbook highlights: - If admitted_series_count drops >40% unexpectedly, revert policy to permissive mode. - For increased CPU >10% across nodes, roll back and switch to sampling-only mode.

Risks & trade-offs: - Edge CPU overhead vs central storage savings; choose conservative default rules to avoid data loss for SLO metrics. - Some tooling downstream expects raw labels; include a mapping table export to reconstruct pre-canonicalized context for debugging.

Docs / artifacts: Link to policy schema and test vectors in attachments.
comments: 2026-02-22 Rafael Ortiz: Spike complete — PoC successfully canonicalized labels for synthetic 10k series down to ~1.8k. CPU overhead measured ~6% on a 8 vCPU node during synthetic load. Next: add trace hook and exemplar deterministic policy.
2026-02-28 Maya Chen (PM): Prioritize ensuring p99 latency metrics are never sampled below 10% retention — added sample_rate_overrides_by_metric acceptance criteria.
2026-03-03 PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/482 (initial exporter + prometheus-proxy). Rafael: needs unit tests for canonicalization and a fuzzer for label regex rules.
2026-03-05 Design review (Anya Patel): Approve the label_rename_map approach, requested UX for a simple mapping table in Console to view pre/post canonicalization for a metric series.
2026-03-08 Security note (Ivan Novak): Confirmed no PII in labels following current rules; recommend an additional rule to blacklist label keys matching 'user_email' patterns. Added to ruleset.
2026-03-10 Rafael Ortiz: Canary deploy started on 12 nodes in us-west-2; parallel-export enabled for 72h. Telemetry dashboards linked in attachments. Monitoring CPU and admitted_series_count closely.
2026-03-10 QA (Leah Brooks): Integration tests added to CI pipeline. Synthetic noisy-workload test shows 64% cardinality reduction with preserved p99 within 2% error margin.
